_comment: Single source of truth for the two population scales used in the SEIR real-data pipeline. Do not hard-code these values anywhere else -- read this file from both R (calibrate_real_5method.R) and Python (bernardo_predict_real.py). See real_data/README_scaling.md for why there are two different scales.
n_bilstm_comment: Population fed to the BiLSTM's 'population_size' input feature. Must stay inside the network's trained range -- see epiworldRcalibrate/inst/models or SEIR_epi_reconstruction test_actual_parameters (2).csv: n in [5000, 10000], recov in [0.071, 0.25]. Values outside this range saturate the sigmoid output head (bug found 2026-08-17: true Utah population, 3.27M, pinned every prediction to the scaler's max regardless of input window).
n_classical_comment: Population used for ABC / ABC-SMC / Nelder-Mead / DE calibration AND for the final run_multiple() CI plot for all 5 methods (including BiLSTM, whose predicted beta is re-simulated at this scale for the plot). Chosen to match the order of magnitude of the real observed case counts (tens per day), exactly like the SIR vignette (N=5000, prevalence = incidence[1]/N) -- NOT derived from Utah's true population. Set to 7000 on 2026-08-17 (user preference; still inside the BiLSTM's trained population range of 5000-10000, see n_bilstm_comment, so both scales stay mutually consistent). Bug found 2026-08-17 (second instance): process_dataset() used to downscale obs by n_classical/n_true (~0.03x when n_classical was 100000) before calibrating, then divide the simulated CI back up by the same factor for plotting. That put the discrete stochastic simulator in a 0/1/2-cases-per-day quantized regime during calibration, and the /0.03 (~x33) rescale then turned every unit of that integer noise into a ~33-case vertical jump in the plotted ribbons/medians -- the sawtooth/staircase artifact reported 2026-08-17. Fix: never scale obs by the true population; only cap n_use at n_classical and seed prevalence directly from the observed window on that same n_classical scale (see process_dataset() in calibrate_real_5method.R).
